description: Structural. Production: uuid5("https://w3id.org/bdchm/Person", str({dbGaP_Subject_ID})). One Person per participant, written once per cohort in person.yaml.
Structural. Production: the dbGaP subject ID as a string. Participant.associated_person points at this Person.

The species, as an NCBITaxon CURIE (CellularOrganismSpeciesEnum is open over NCBITaxon, so it has no fixed list). Every human cohort writes NCBITaxon:9606 (Homo sapiens); production does this in all 11 cohorts.
Not used for human cohorts. Leave empty.
Calendar year of birth (integer). dbGaP releases rarely carry it; leave empty unless the source gives the year. Never derive it from age plus an unknown exam date.

Concept: Death. Write the VitalStatusEnum name (ALIVE, DEAD). Whether the participant is alive or dead at the end of the study's follow-up; Person has no date or visit, so this is the latest known status. Rules: (1) A death indicator maps directly (dead/yes to DEAD, alive/no to ALIVE). (2) A death-record table that has rows only for people who died: write DEAD when the record exists and leave the slot empty otherwise; never infer ALIVE from the absence of a death record (production ARIC, CARDIA). (3) 'Pending adjudication' of cause does not change vital status. (4) There is no UNKNOWN value; leave the slot empty when status is not known. The transform spec accepts either the enum name or its meaning CURIE, and the ingest is expected to emit the CURIE.
Showing characteristics of life (NCIt). Meaning OMOP:4230556. Either the enum name or the meaning CURIE (OMOP:4230556) is accepted in the transform spec, and the ingest is expected to emit the CURIE.
The cessation of life (NCIt). Meaning OMOP:434489. Either the enum name or the meaning CURIE (OMOP:434489) is accepted in the transform spec, and the ingest is expected to emit the CURIE.

Age at death in integer days since birth. Production converts years with x 365 (ARIC 'COMPUTED AGE AT DEATH' x 365). When the source gives age at enrollment and days from enrollment to death, production adds them (WHI: age at screening x 365 + days enrollment to death), which is more precise than whole years. Leave empty for participants who are not dead.
Example source variable description: A. Information from Death Index/Certificate. COMPUTED AGE AT DEATH Q10 [Death Certificate Form]|Days enrollment to All Discovered Death|Age at screening

description: Calendar year of death (integer). dbGaP releases rarely carry it; leave empty unless the source gives the year.

Concept: Cause of death. A list of CauseOfDeath objects (one per recorded cause). Rules: (1) Do not prefix raw death-certificate codes blindly; detect the ICD revision first. Letter-led codes valid in ICD-10-CM keep the ICD10CM: prefix. ICD-9 numeric codes (e.g. 162.9) are converted to ICD-10-CM with the CMS crosswalk. WHO-only ICD-10 codes with no ICD-10-CM equivalent (e.g. I64, I50.0) are mapped to the closest ICD-10-CM code, best effort. All proposed conversions go to Anne for review before use. Decide the revision from the source, not from the first character alone: CARDIA ZTDCICD and numeric ARIC codes are ICD-9, and letter-led ICD-9-CM external-cause codes such as E858.8 are ICD-9 too (E858.8 is not an ICD-10-CM code). ICD-9 E and V codes go through the CMS crosswalk like numeric codes. (2) Underlying cause is order 1; contributing causes follow in source order (2, 3, ...). (3) Adjudicated categories (CHS CAUSE80, MESA dthtype, WHI DEATHALLCAUSE) have no single ICD code: production maps them to an ICD-10 block or category (e.g. 'ATHEROSCLEROTIC CHD' to ICD10CM:I20-I25, 'Breast Cancer' to ICD10CM:C50); a block range is not a single ICD-10-CM code (see questions). The MESA non-cardiovascular death types go to the cohorts for review (issue to be raised). (4) Death certificates coded in ICD-9 or ICD-8 (CARDIA, FHS) are written by production as ICD9CM: or ICD8CM:, which are outside BDC-HM's ICD-10-CM range (see questions). ICD-9 is superseded by rule 1. ICD-8 codes (FHS) are mapped by hand to ICD-10-CM and reviewed by Anne before use; the FHS cause-of-death table has no ICD-revision variable, so confirm the revision first (for example from the death date). (5) Unknown or ill-defined cause: production MESA uses ICD10CM:R99. MESA dthtype 5 ('NON-CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE'), 9 ('NON-CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (INELIGIBLE FOR REVIEW)') and 999 ('PENDING ADJUDICATION') leave cause empty. (6) A cause-of-death variable can also support a Condition with condition_provenance DEATH_RECORD; recording it here does not replace that.
Example source variable description: Death Eligibility Check Section. UNDERLYING CAUSE OF DEATH CODE Q18 [Death Certificate Form]|A. Information from Death Index/Certificate. 1ST DEATH CERTIFICATE ICD CODE Q19A [Death Certificate Form]|CAUSE OF DEATH CODE: ICD-9 1|CAUSE OF DEATH|DEATH TYPE|Cause of All Discovered Death|UNDERLYING CAUSE OF DEATH

description: Required. One cause as a CURIE from CauseOfDeathEnum, which BDC-HM defines as ICD-10-CM (prefix ICD10CM:). Use the most specific code the source supports. Detect the code's ICD revision before writing it; see cause_of_death rule (1).
Example source variable description: A. Information from Death Index/Certificate. 1ST DEATH CERTIFICATE ICD CODE Q19A [Death Certificate Form]|A. Information from Death Index/Certificate. 2ND DEATH CERTIFICATE ICD CODE Q19B [Death Certificate Form]

description: Required. Integer rank: 1 = underlying or primary cause; 2 and up = additional or contributing causes in the order the source lists them.
Example source variable description: UNDERLYING CAUSE OF DEATH|1ST CONTRIBUTING CAUSE OF DEATH
